translation_direction: en → vi; direct from the specifically identified complete English electronic witness
ai_disclosure: Direct AI-produced Vietnamese prose by Claude Opus 5.5. The drafting system conducted the final full assessment; a separate-context assessment by the same model family read every pair and supplied findings first. No human translator, editor, reviewer, independent model consensus or actual reader feedback is recorded.

entry_conditions: Complete named-source and Vietnamese texts, explicit alignment and exact content hashes.
Compare every source and target passage; disclose that this assessor also revised the text and has seen earlier AI assessments.
Source and target edition titles are present and compared explicitly; the title review must match both catalog title strings exactly.
exit_conditions: One complete AI review with a weighted score at least 8.6 using the five unchanged weights and half-point category scores; no separate numerical dimension floors.
All canonical passages reviewed; no unresolved major or critical finding; source and target hashes match the final text.
Publication and rights status are recorded separately in the edition catalog; an AI score does not supply a license.
The selected review includes source_title, target_title and a substantive title rationale; changed titles require a fresh matching review.
review_process.human_feedback: Optional after publication or while a work remains a draft; no prior human publication review is required by v2.

decisions.decision: Lockwood’s affected narration and Nelly’s plainer voice are kept distinct; secondary narrators (Isabella’s letter, Zillah) keep their own registers.
decisions.rationale: The nested narration is the novel’s structure.

decisions.decision: Brontë’s passionate, dense prose and long periods are kept; em dashes unspaced as in the source; the ballad stanza kept as verse.

revision_history.scope: Complete initial direct translation, separate-context full source/target assessment and concrete revisions before the selected final review.

changes.explanation: Joseph’s ‘Him as allas maks a third’ (the Devil) had been given the honorific Đấng reserved for God; corrected.

Dialect and idiom misreadings corrected: Yorkshire ‘starved’ (chilled), ‘thrashing him to a mummy’, ‘struggled into its teens’, ‘If he had caught me!’, ‘kick the breath out of him’, ‘a stone or two heavier’.

Book-wide rulings across twelve drafting parts: curate, the fold, library, shilling, Bible names; Nelly’s cậu for young Hindley and adult Hareton, ông to Heathcliff; cô/nàng for young Catherine by chapter; Heathcliff’s nàng for the elder Catherine; Joseph’s mi and restored dialect.
Kinship corrected (Linton is not young Catherine’s elder cousin), Hareton’s age, and about twenty calques and stiff phrasings.

selection_limit: Chosen for a complete, directly sourced and openly reusable Vietnamese edition. Existing Vietnamese translations, their quality and reader demand have not been comprehensively assessed; no absence or superiority claim is made.

glossary.draft_rendering: Đồi Gió Hú / Trang trại Thrushcross
glossary.rationale: The established Vietnamese names; ‘the Heights’ and ‘the Grange’ follow them.

glossary.draft_rendering: rustic Central-Vietnamese-tinged speech (tau/mi/bây, răng, rứa, chi, nờ)
glossary.rationale: Marks his dialect and sanctimony while staying comprehensible; Bible names in hyphenated Protestant spelling.

glossary.source_term: address: Heathcliff ↔ Catherine; Nelly; young Catherine; Linton; uncles
glossary.draft_rendering: tớ/cậu in childhood, anh/em as adults; Nelly ông/chị with Heathcliff; young Catherine chị to Linton; Edgar cậu, Heathcliff dượng; Heathcliff ta/cháu to his niece, then tao/mày after the lock-in
glossary.rationale: Vietnamese kinship and register track the novel’s two generations and the turn to open cruelty.

glossary.draft_rendering: “Nelly, em chính là Heathcliff!”; “…những người ngủ dưới lớp đất yên lành ấy lại có thể ngủ không yên.”
glossary.rationale: Fixed renderings of the novel’s best-known lines.

witness_decision: Selected the complete text of Project Gutenberg #768. Gutenberg does not identify the printed edition transcribed; the novel was first published by Thomas Cautley Newby in December 1847. Not collated with a print facsimile; italic emphasis is not preserved in plain canonical passages.

unresolved_questions.explanation: Hareton’s contemptuous thee/thou is rendered with polite tôi/cô in one early scene.

title_review.rationale: Đồi gió hú is the long-established Vietnamese title; inside the text the house is the proper name Đồi Gió Hú.

passage_assessment_notes.assessment: The ghost at the window and Heathcliff’s cry.
Final sentence in its fixed rendering.
